argv filtering. On a device there is no argv: RFC-0045 resolves boot config from baked values and the board.

phase-467 Row 11 follow-through (2026-10-03) -- CORRECTED. "there is no argv" was the whole reason, and it stopped being true on a hosted build: since #1591 the RUST entries (`nros::init_with_args` / `nros::Context::new`) parse `--ros-args` and honour `-r`. The C++ surface still has nothing to strip -- `rclcpp::init(argc, argv)` calls no parser and ABORTS on `--ros-args` (`NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_INIT_ARGV`, `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp`), so a C++ caller never hands ROS arguments past `init` that this would remove. Stays `absent` until a C++ entry parses; the Rust parse already scopes `--ros-args ... --` itself, so the program's own arguments are never mistaken for ROS ones.

phase-467 Row 11, C++ half (2026-10-05) -- the sentence above went stale two days later: `rclcpp::init(argc, argv)` no longer aborts on `--ros-args`, it honours `-r` and refuses the rest (see `cpp:init`). Still `absent`, and the reason is now the real one: rclcpp's `remove_ros_arguments` exists so a program can hand ITS OWN parser an argv without the ROS tokens. Our parse already scopes `--ros-args ... --` itself and ignores everything outside, so nothing upstream of a user's parser needs stripping; and a returned `std::vector<std::string>` has no freestanding spelling (RFC-0096). Adopt it when a user asks for it.
